ability.e: This phone has the ability to have its software upgraded wirelessly.

abroad.e: A tree spreads its branches abroad.

accept.d: To receive, especially with a consent, with favour, or with approval.
accept.e: The Boy Scouts were going to accept him as a member.

acceptable.d: Worthy, decent, sure of being accepted or received with at least moderate pleasure
acceptable.e: We need to find an acceptable present for Jeff.

accident.d: An unexpected event with negative consequences occurring without the intention of the one suffering the consequences, and (in the strict sense) not directly caused by humans.
accident.e: to die by an accident such as an act of God

account.d: A registry of pecuniary transactions; a written or printed statement of business dealings or debts and credits, and also of other things subjected to a reckoning or review.
account.e: to keep one's account at the bank.

achieve.d: To succeed in something, now especially in academic performance.

across.d: To, toward, or from the far side of (something that lies between two points of interest).

actually.d: (modal) In act or in fact; really; in truth; positively.
actually.e: Actually, I had nothing to do with that incident.

addition.e: The addition of five more items to the agenda will make the meeting unbearably long.

adjust.e: Morimoto's recipes are adjusted to suit the American palate.

admire.d: To be amazed at; to view with surprise; to marvel at.

admit.d: To allow to enter; to grant entrance (to), whether into a place, into the mind, or into consideration.
admit.e: to admit a serious thought into the mind

adult.d: A fully grown human or animal.
adult.e: an adult human, animal, or plant

advantage.d: Any condition, circumstance, opportunity or means, particularly favorable to success, or to any desired end.
advantage.e: The enemy had the advantage of a more elevated position.

adventure.d: The encountering of risks; a bold undertaking, in which dangers are likely to be encountered, and the issue is staked upon unforeseen events; a daring feat.

advertisement.d: A commercial solicitation designed to sell some commodity, service or similar.
advertisement.e: The city council placed an advertisement in the local newspaper to inform its residents of the forthcoming roadworks.

advertising.d: To give (especially public) notice of (something); to announce publicly.
advertising.e: For personal needs, advertise on the internet or in a local newspaper.

advise.d: To give advice to; to offer an opinion to, as worthy or expedient to be followed.
advise.e: The dentist advised me to brush three times a day.

affair.d: (often in the plural) Something which is done or is to be done; business of any kind, commercial, professional, or public.

against.e: It is hard work to swim against the current.

aged.e: I knocked on the door and an aged man opened it.

agent.d: One who exerts power, or has the power to act.
agent.e: He worked as an agent for the government.

ahead.d: At or towards the front; in the direction one is facing or moving.

air.d: The substance constituting earth's atmosphere, particularly:
air.e: I'm going outside to get some air.

aisle.d: A wing of a building, notably in a church separated from the nave proper by piers.

alarm.d: A summons to arms, as on the approach of an enemy.
alarm.e: The sudden drop in temperature should alarm you into taking precautions.

alarm clock.d: A clock designed to sound an alert at a preset time, primarily to wake someone from sleep.

alive.e: As long as the plant is alive, he will continue to water it.

allow.d: To grant, give, admit, accord, afford, or yield; to let one have.
allow.e: to allow a servant his liberty;  to allow a free passage;  to allow one day for rest

alright.d: Alternative form of all right; satisfactory; okay; in acceptable order.

ambition.d: Eager or inordinate desire for some object that confers distinction, as preferment, honor, superiority, political power, or fame; desire to distinguish one's self from other people.
ambition.e: My daughter, Johanna, wants to be a firefighter very much. She has a lot of ambition.

among.d: Denotes a mingling or intermixing with distinct or separable objects. (See Usage Note at amidst.)
among.e: How can you speak with authority about their customs when you have never lived among them?

amused.d: simple past and past participle of amuse
amused.e: While waiting for the bus, I amused myself by performing a mime interpretation of the Gettysburg Address.

ancestor.d: One from whom a person is descended, whether on the father's or mother's side, at any distance of time; a progenitor; a forefather; a forebear.
ancestor.e: This fossil animal is regarded as the ancestor of the horse.

ancient.d: A person who is very old.
ancient.e: an ancient city  an ancient forest

angel.d: An incorporeal and holy or semidivine messenger from a deity or other divine entity, traditionally depicted as a youthful, winged figure in flowing robes. One of the lowest order of such beings, below virtues.

angrily.d: In an angry manner; under the influence of anger.
angrily.e: "Leave me alone for once," she said angrily.

ankle.d: The skeletal joint which connects the foot with the leg; the uppermost portion of the foot and lowermost portion of the leg, which contain this skeletal joint.

anniversary.d: A day that is an exact number of years (to the day) since a given significant event occurred. Often preceded by an ordinal number indicating the number of years.
anniversary.e: Today is the fiftieth anniversary of the end of the war.

annoy.d: To disturb or irritate, especially by continued or repeated acts; to bother with unpleasant deeds.
annoy.e: to annoy an army by impeding its march, or by a cannonade

annoying.d: To disturb or irritate, especially by continued or repeated acts; to bother with unpleasant deeds.

anxious.e: I could tell she was anxious as she was biting her nails.

anyway.e: He didn't enjoy washing his car, but it was so dirty that he did it anyway.

anywhere.d: In or at any location or an unknown location.
anywhere.e: I don't know where I left my keys. They could be anywhere.

apart.d: (Used after a noun or in the predicate) Exceptional, distinct.

apartment.d: A complete domicile occupying only part of a building, especially one for rent; a flat.

apologise.d: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of apologize.

apologize.d: To make an apology or excuse; to acknowledge some fault or offense, with expression of regret for it, by way of amends
apologize.e: My correspondent apologized for not answering my letter.

apparently.e: A man may be apparently friendly, yet malicious in heart.

appear.d: To come or be in sight; to be in view; to become visible.
appear.e: A great writer appeared at that time.

appearance.d: The act of appearing or coming into sight; the act of becoming visible to the eye.

apply.d: To lay or place; to put (one thing to another)
apply.e: to apply cream to a rash

appointment.d: The act of appointing a person to hold an office or to have a position of trust.
appointment.e: His appointment as treasurer was deemed suitable.

appreciate.d: To be grateful or thankful for.

appropriate.e: Let no man appropriate the use of a common benefit.

architecture.d: The art and science of designing and managing the construction of buildings and other structures, particularly if they are well proportioned and decorated.
architecture.e: Architecture is the visual public expression of a culture’s achievements, values, and outlook. ― Max Roscoe, "How Your City Is Killing You With Ugliness"

area.d: A measure of the extent of a surface; it is measured in square units.

argue.d: To show grounds for concluding (that); to indicate, imply.
argue.e: He also argued for stronger methods to be used against China.

argument.d: A fact or statement used to support a proposition; a reason.

armchair.d: A chair with supports for the arms or elbows.

artificial.d: Man-made; made by humans; of artifice.
artificial.e: The flowers were artificial, and he thought them rather tacky.

asleep.d: In a state of sleep; also, broadly, resting.
asleep.e: I was asleep when you called.

assistant.d: Someone who is present; a bystander, a witness.

astronaut.d: A member of the crew of a spaceship or other spacecraft that travels beyond Earth's atmosphere, or someone trained to serve that purpose.

athlete.d: A participant in a group of sporting activities which includes track and field, road running, cross country running and racewalking.
athlete.e: She's the first athlete in her sport to obtain a corporate sponsor.

atom.d: The smallest possible amount of matter which still retains its identity as a chemical element, now known to consist of a nucleus surrounded by electrons.

attack.d: An attempt to cause damage, injury to, or death of opponent or enemy.
attack.e: They claimed the censorship of the article was an attack on free speech.

attempt.d: The action of trying at something.

attention.e: Please direct your attention to the following words.

attitude.d: The position of the body or way of carrying oneself.
attitude.e: The ballet dancer walked with a graceful attitude.

attractive.d: Causing attraction; having the quality of attracting by inherent force.

audience.d: A group of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a performance, speech, etc.
audience.e: We joined the audience just as the lights went down.

audio.d: A sound, or a sound signal

author.d: The originator or creator of a work, especially of a literary composition.
author.e: Have you read any Corinthian authors?

automatic.e: I never learned to drive a stick. I can only drive an automatic.

avoid.d: To try not to meet or communicate with (a person); to shun
avoid.e: I try to avoid the company of gamblers.

award.d: A judgment, sentence, or final decision. Specifically: The decision of arbitrators in a case submitted.
award.e: Four or five of these medals are awarded every year.

background.d: One's social heritage, or previous life; what one did in the past.
background.e: The lawyer had a background in computer science.

badly.e: Things are going badly for her: she did badly in her exams owing to a badly designed studying schedule.

badminton.d: A racquet sport played indoors on a court by two opposing players (singles) or two opposing pairs of players (doubles), in which a shuttlecock is volleyed over a net and the competitions are presided by an umpire in British English and a referee in American English.

bake.d: The act of cooking food by baking.
bake.e: I baked a delicious cherry pie.

balcony.d: An accessible structure extending from a building, especially outside a window.

balloon.d: An inflatable buoyant object, often (but not necessarily) round and flexible.
balloon.e: His stomach ballooned from eating such a large meal.

banking.d: The business of managing a bank.

barbecue.d: A fireplace or pit for grilling food, typically used outdoors and traditionally employing hot charcoal as the heating medium.
barbecue.e: We cooked our food on the barbecue.

bargain.d: An agreement between parties concerning the sale of property; or a contract by which one party binds themself to transfer the right to some property for a consideration, and the other party binds themself to receive the property and pay the consideration.
bargain.e: They had to bargain for a few minutes to get a decent price for the rug.

base.d: Something from which other things extend; a foundation. A supporting, lower or bottom component of a structure or object.
base.e: Troops have been based in Munich since the end of World War II.

basic.d: A necessary commodity, a staple requirement.
basic.e: Rice is a basic for many Asian villagers.

basically.d: In a fundamental, essential or basic manner
basically.e: They've added some fancy features, but it's basically still a car.

basket.d: A lightweight container, generally round, open at the top, and tapering toward the bottom.
basket.e: A basket of fake fruit adorned the table.

batch.d: The quantity of bread or other baked goods baked at one time.
batch.e: We made a batch of cookies to take to the party.

been.d: A flying insect, of the clade Anthophila within the hymenopteran superfamily Apoidea, known for its organised societies (though only a minority have them), for collecting pollen and (in some species) producing wax and honey.

beer.d: An alcoholic drink fermented from starch material, commonly barley malt; often with hops or some other substance (like gruit) to impart a bitter flavor.
beer.e: Beer is brewed all over the world.

beg.d: The act of begging; an imploring request.
beg.e: He begged on the street corner from passers-by.

beginning.d: The act of doing that which begins anything; commencement of an action, state, or space of time; entrance into being or upon a course; the first act, effort, or state of a succession of acts or states.

behavior.d: Human conduct relative to social norms.

behaviour.d: The way a living creature behaves or acts.
behaviour.e: She can't stop the strange behaviour because she has OCD (obsessive-compulsive disorder).

belly.e: You've grown a belly over Christmas! Time to join the gym again.

belt.d: A band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants), hold weapons (such as a gun or sword), or serve as a decorative piece of clothing.
belt.e: As part of the act, the fat clown's belt broke, causing his pants to fall down.

bend.e: There's a sharp bend in the road ahead.

beyond.e: She had no reason for the conviction beyond the very inadequate one that she had seen him around London.

blanket.d: A heavy, loosely woven fabric, usually large and woollen, used for warmth while sleeping or resting.
blanket.e: The baby was cold, so his mother put a blanket over him.

blood.d: A vital liquid flowing in the bodies of many types of animals that usually conveys nutrients and oxygen. In vertebrates, it is colored red by hemoglobin, is conveyed by arteries and veins, is pumped by the heart and is usually generated in bone marrow.
blood.e: Some insects are known for consuming blood.

bloom.d: A blossom; the flower of a plant; an expanded bud.

board game.d: Any of many games of strategy or chance played on a specially designed board; often involves one or more players moving pieces and using dice or cards.

boil.d: A localized accumulation of pus in the skin, resulting from infection.
boil.e: Add the noodles when the water comes to the boil.

boiled.d: (of liquids) To heat to the point where it begins to turn into a gas.
boiled.e: Boil some water in a pan.

bonus.d: Something extra that is good; an added benefit.
bonus.e: The employee of the week receives a bonus for his excellent work.

bookcase.d: A piece of furniture for the storage and display of books.

bookshelf.d: A shelf or shelves for storing books for easy visual reference.

boss.d: A person who oversees and directs the work of others; a supervisor.
boss.e: Chat turned to whisper when the boss entered the conference room.

bother.d: To annoy, to disturb, to irritate; to be troublesome to, to make trouble for.
bother.e: Would it bother you if I smoked?

bra.d: An item of clothing, usually underwear worn to support the breasts.

brainstorm.d: To investigate something, or solve a problem using brainstorming.
brainstorm.e: I had been working on the problem for weeks, and then I had a brainstorm and saw that the solution was easy.

brake.d: A device used to slow or stop the motion of a wheel, or of a vehicle, usually by friction (although other resistive forces, such as electromagnetic fields or aerodynamic drag, can also be used); also, the controls or apparatus used to engage such a mechanism such as the pedal in a car.
brake.e: Give the car a quick brake.

branch.d: The woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing.
branch.e: the branch of an antler, a chandelier, or a railway

brand.e: The ranch hands had to brand every new calf by lunchtime.

brave.e: After braving tricks on the high-dive, he braved a jump off the first diving platform.

breeze.e: The breeze rustled the papers on her desk.

bride.d: A woman in the context of her own wedding; one who is going to marry or has just been married.

brilliant.e: the brilliant lights along the promenade

budget.d: The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or time-frame.
budget.e: We flew on a budget airline.

bug.d: An insect of the order Hemiptera (the “true bugs”).
bug.e: These flies are a bother. I’ll get some bug spray and kill them.

bulb.d: The bulb-shaped underground portion of a plant such as a tulip, consisting of a shortened stem and many fleshy scale leaves, from which the rest of the plant may be regrown.

burn.d: A physical injury caused by heat, cold, electricity, radiation or caustic chemicals.
burn.e: chili burn from eating hot peppers

bury.e: bury a bone;  bury the embers

bus station.d: A major bus stop, one that serves as a transfer point between a large number of routes.

bus stop.d: A place where public transport buses stop to allow passengers to board or leave.
bus stop.e: He was waiting at the bus stop with her.

bush.d: A woody plant distinguished from a tree by its multiple stems and lower height, being usually less than six metres tall; a horticultural rather than strictly botanical category.

businessman.d: A man in business, one who works at a commercial institution.

cafeteria.d: A restaurant in which customers select their food at a counter then carry it on a tray to a table to eat

calendar.d: Any system by which time is divided into days, weeks, months, and years.
calendar.e: Write his birthday on the calendar hanging on the wall.

camping.d: present participle and gerund of camp
camping.e: Camping is a favorite summer activity.

campus.d: The grounds or property of a school, college, university, business, church, or hospital, often understood to include buildings and other structures.
campus.e: The campus is sixty hectares in size.

capital.d: Money and wealth: the means to acquire or produce goods and services, especially in a non-barter system.
capital.e: He does not have enough capital to start a business.

captain.e: The captain is the last man to leave a sinking ship.

car park.d: An outdoor area or a building where cars may be parked.

carrot.d: A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, family Apiaceae, especially the subspecies sativus.

cash.d: Money in the form of notes or bills and coins, as opposed to checks, credit or electronic transactions.
cash.e: How are you off for cash? After you bounced those checks last time, they want to be paid in cash.

cassette.d: A small flat case containing magnetic tape on two reels, used to record and play back audio and video material.

castle.d: A large building that is fortified and contains many defences; in previous ages often inhabited by a nobleman or king.

cause.d: (often with of, typically of adverse results) The source of, or reason for, an event or action; that which produces or effects a result.
cause.e: They identified a burst pipe as the cause of the flooding.

center.d: The point in the interior of a circle that is equidistant from all points on the circumference.
center.e: He centered the heading of the document.

cereal.d: A type of grass (such as wheat, rice or oats) cultivated for its edible grains.

certain.e: I was certain of my decision.

certainly.d: In a way which is certain; with certainty.
certainly.e: That was certainly sweet of him.

chain.d: A series of interconnected rings or links usually made of metal.
chain.e: He wore a gold chain around the neck.

challenge.e: We challenged the boys next door to a game of football.

chance.e: We had the chance to meet the president last week.

chat.d: To be engaged in informal conversation.

chef.d: The presiding cook in the kitchen of a large household.

chemical.d: Any specific chemical element or chemical compound or alloy.

chess.d: A board game for two players with each beginning with sixteen chess pieces moving according to fixed rules across a chessboard with the objective to checkmate the opposing king.

chili.d: The pungent, spicy fresh or dried fruit of any of several cultivated varieties of capsicum peppers, used in cooking.

chin.d: The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.

choice.d: An option; a decision; an opportunity to choose or select something.
choice.e: Do I have a choice of what color to paint it?

cigarette.d: Tobacco or other substances, in a thin roll wrapped with paper, intended to be smoked.

claim.d: A demand of ownership made for something.

clear.d: Full extent; distance between extreme limits; especially; the distance between the nearest surfaces of two bodies, or the space between walls.
clear.e: a room ten feet square in the clear

clerk.d: One who occupationally works with records, accounts, letters, etc.; an office worker.
clerk.e: The law school graduate clerked for the supreme court judge for the summer.

click.d: A brief, sharp, not particularly loud, relatively high-pitched sound produced by the impact of something small and hard against something hard, such as by the operation of a switch, a lock, or a latch.
click.e: As I turned the key, the lock gave a click and the door opened.

climbing.d: The sport of climbing, ascending a wall or a rock or another object using available holds, generally with the safety of a rope and belayer.
climbing.e: The next day, the team had to wear special ice climbing footwear while repairing other research devices on the glacier.

clone.d: A living organism (originally a plant) produced asexually from a single ancestor, to which it is genetically identical.
clone.e: This new species is a clone of the mimosa plant.

clown.d: A slapstick performance artist often associated with a circus and usually characterized by bright, oversized clothing, a red nose, face paint, and a brightly colored wig.
clown.e: He was regarded as the clown of the school, always playing pranks.

clue.d: A strand of yarn etc. as used to guide one through a labyrinth; something which points the way, a guide.
clue.e: The crossword compiler wasn't sure how to clue the word "should".

coast.d: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
coast.e: The rocky coast of Maine has few beaches.

coin.d: (money) A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.

cola.d: The kola plant, genus Cola, famous for its nut, or one of these nuts.

column.d: A solid upright structure designed usually to support a larger structure above it, such as a roof or horizontal beam, but sometimes for decoration.

comb.d: A toothed implement for grooming the hair or (formerly) for keeping it in place.
comb.e: I need to comb my hair before we leave the house

comfortable.d: A stuffed or quilted coverlet for a bed; a comforter.
comfortable.e: This is the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in.

commitment.d: The act or an instance of committing, putting in charge, keeping, or trust, especially:

committee.d: A body of one or more persons convened for the accomplishment of some specific purpose, typically with formal protocols.
committee.e: My uncle is on the committee.

common.d: Mutual good, shared by more than one.
common.e: The two competitors have the common aim of winning the championship.

communicate.d: To impart. To impart or transmit (information or knowledge) to someone; to make known, to tell.
communicate.e: It is vital that I communicate this information to you.

communication.d: The act or fact of communicating anything; transmission.

company.d: A team; a group of people who work together professionally.

comparative.e: He gave us a comparative example to illustrate how the human mind works.

compare.d: To assess the similarities and differences between two or more things ["to compare X with Y"]. Having made the comparison of X with Y, one might have found it similar to Y or different from Y.
compare.e: Compare the tiger's coloration with that of the zebra.

competition.e: The competition for this job is strong.

complain.d: To express feelings of pain, dissatisfaction, or resentment.
complain.e: Joe was always complaining about the noise made by his neighbours.

complaint.e: I have no complaints about the quality of his work, but I don't enjoy his company.

complete.d: To finish; to make done; to reach the end.
complete.e: My life will be complete once I buy this new television.

composer.d: One who composes; an author. Especially, one who composes music.

concentrate.d: A substance that is in a condensed form.
concentrate.e: to concentrate rays of light into a focus

concern.d: That which affects one’s welfare or happiness. A matter of interest to someone. The adposition before the matter of interest is usually over, about or for.
concern.e: Judy's eyes filled with concern as she listened to the news report.

condition.d: A logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false.
condition.e: Environmental protection is a condition for sustainability.   What other planets might have the right conditions for life?   The union had a dispute over sick time and other conditions of employment.

confident.d: A person in whom one can confide or share one's secrets: a friend.
confident.e: I'm pretty confident that she's not lying, she's acting normally.

consequence.d: That which follows something on which it depends; that which is produced by a cause.
consequence.e: I'm warning you. If you don't get me the report on time, there will be consequences.

consider.e: Consider that we’ve had three major events and the year has hardly begun.

contact.d: The act of touching physically; being in close association.
contact.e: I haven't been in contact with her for years.

container.d: Someone who contains; something that contains.

context.d: The surroundings, circumstances, environment, background or settings that determine, specify, or clarify the meaning of an event or other occurrence.
context.e: —In what context did your attack on him happen? —We had a pretty tense relationship at the time, and when he insulted me I snapped.

continent.d: One of the main contiguous landmasses, separated by water or geological features, on the surface of a planet, sometimes including its continental shelves and the islands on them.

continue.e: Shall I continue speaking, or will you just interrupt me again?

contrast.d: A difference in lightness, brightness and/or hue between two colours that makes them more or less distinguishable.

control.e: The government has complete control over the situation.

convenience.e: Fast food is popular because of its cost and convenience.

convenient.d: Serving to reduce a difficulty, or accessible with minimum difficulty; expedient.
convenient.e: Fast food might be convenient, but it's also very unhealthy.

cooking.d: The process of preparing food by using heat.
cooking.e: I filled the cooking pot with water, and poured some cooking sherry into the skillet.

cost.d: To incur a charge of; to require payment of a (specified) price.
cost.e: It will cost you a lot of money to take a trip around the world.

couple.d: Two partners in a romantic or sexual relationship.
couple.e: I've coupled our system to theirs.

crazy.e: His ideas were both frightening and crazy.

credit.d: Reliance on the truth of something said or done; faith; trust.
credit.e: He arrived five minutes late, but to his credit he did work an extra ten minutes at the end of his shift.

cricket.d: An insect in the order Orthoptera, especially family Gryllidae, that makes a chirping sound by rubbing its wing casings against combs on its hind legs.

crime.d: A specific act committed in violation of the law.

criticize.e: They criticized him for endangering people's lives.

cross.d: A geometrical figure consisting of two straight lines or bars intersecting each other such that at least one of them is bisected by the other.
cross.e: Put a cross for a wrong answer and a tick for a right one.

crowd.d: A group of people congregated or collected into a close body without order.
crowd.e: After the movie let out, a crowd of people pushed through the exit doors.

cruise.d: A sea or lake voyage, especially one taken for pleasure.

cupboard.d: A board or table used to openly hold and display silver plate and other dishware; a sideboard; a buffet.

custom.d: Frequent repetition of the same behavior; way of behavior common to many; ordinary manner; habitual practice; method of doing, living or behaving.
custom.e: My feet are very large, so I need custom shoes.

dangerous.e: Railway crossings without gates are highly dangerous.

daylight.d: The natural light that is ambient in daytime, being mostly sunlight (both direct and indirect, on either sunny days or cloudy days).
daylight.e: In those days the entire factory was lit only by daylight and was closed at night.

dead.e: All of my grandparents are dead.

deal.d: A division, a portion, a share.
deal.e: We gave three deals of grain in tribute to the king.

death.d: The cessation of life and all associated processes; the end of an organism's existence as an entity independent from its environment and its return to an inert, non-living state.
death.e: My grandfather died/met a violent death, which saddened the whole family.

debate.d: To participate in a debate; to dispute, argue, especially in a public arena.
debate.e: "Debate me, coward!" snarled the completely normal intellectual.

decide.d: To resolve (a contest, problem, dispute, etc.); to choose, determine, or settle
decide.e: Her last-minute goal decided the game.

deep.d: (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc.

deeply.d: To a deep extent or degree; very greatly.
deeply.e: I am deeply concerned about this matter.

degree.d: A stage of proficiency or qualification in a course of study, now especially an award bestowed by a university or, in some countries, a college, as a certification of academic achievement. (In the United States, can include secondary schools.)
degree.e: She has two bachelor's degrees and is studying towards a master's degree.

delay.d: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.
delay.e: the delay before the echo of a sound

dentist.d: A medical doctor who specializes in teeth.

department store.d: A large store containing many different departments, each of which deals in the sale of different goods or services.

depend.d: (followed by on or upon, formerly also by of) To be contingent or conditioned; to have something as a necessary condition; to hinge on.
depend.e: we depend on the mailman to come at the usual time.

description.d: A sketch or account of anything in words; a portraiture or representation in language; an enumeration of the essential qualities of a thing or species.

desert.d: (usually in the plural) That which is deserved or merited; a just punishment or reward

dessert.d: A sweet confection served as the last course of a meal

destroy.d: To damage beyond use or repair.

detail.d: Something small enough to escape casual notice.
detail.e: Note this fine detail in the lower left corner.

develop.d: To change with a specific direction, progress.
develop.e: Let's see how things develop and then make our decision.

diamond.d: A glimmering glass-like mineral that is an allotrope of carbon in which each atom is surrounded by four others in the form of a tetrahedron.
diamond.e: The saw is coated with diamond.

diary.d: A daily log of experiences, especially those of the writer.
diary.e: They kept separate diaries. His was on paper and her diary was on her computer's hard drive.

die.d: To stop living; to become dead; to undergo death.

diet.d: The food and beverage a person or animal consumes.
diet.e: The diet of the Giant Panda consists mainly of bamboo.

differently.e: Things turned out differently from what I'd envisaged.

difficulty.d: The state of being difficult, or hard to do.
difficulty.e: We faced a difficulty in trying to book a flight so late.

digital camera.d: An electronic, often battery-powered device for recording and storing photographs in digital format, especially on a flash card.

dinosaur.d: Those animals of the clade Dinosauria that existed during the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods and are now extinct.
dinosaur.e: Despite what some cartoons portray, no humans were around when dinosaurs roamed the Earth.

direct.e: to direct the affairs of a nation or the movements of an army

direction.d: A theoretical line (physically or mentally) followed from a point of origin or towards a destination. May be relative (e.g. up, left, outbound, dorsal), geographical (e.g. north), rotational (e.g. clockwise), or with respect to an object or location (e.g. toward Boston).
direction.e: Keep going in the same direction.

director.d: One who directs; the person in charge of managing a department or directorate (e.g., director of engineering), project, or production (as in a show or film, e.g., film director).

disadvantage.d: A weakness or undesirable characteristic; a con.
disadvantage.e: The disadvantage to owning a food processor is that you have to store it somewhere.

disagree.d: To fail to agree; to have a different opinion or belief.
disagree.e: My results in the laboratory consistently disagree with yours.

disappointed.d: To sadden or displease (someone) by underperforming, or by not delivering something promised or hoped for.
disappointed.e: His lack of respect disappointed her.

disappointing.e: disappointing results / news; a disappointing experience

disco.e: You don't need to worry about these details at the complaint stage, we can get them in disco.

discover.d: To find or learn something for the first time.
discover.e: Turning the corner, I discovered a lovely little shop. I discovered that they sold widgets.

discussion.d: Conversation or debate concerning a particular topic.
discussion.e: My discussion with the professor was very enlightening.

dislike.d: An attitude or a feeling of distaste or aversion.
dislike.e: Tell me your likes and dislikes.

display.e: The trapeze artist put on an amazing acrobatic display.

disturb.d: to confuse a quiet, constant state or a calm, continuous flow, in particular: thoughts, actions or liquids.
disturb.e: The noisy ventilation disturbed me during the exam.

divide.d: To split or separate (something) into two or more parts.
divide.e: Stay on your side of the divide, please.

dizzy.e: I stood up too fast and felt dizzy.

done.d: Having completed or finished an activity.
done.e: He pushed his empty plate away, sighed and pronounced "I am done."

double.d: Made up of two matching or complementary elements.

doubt.d: Disbelief or uncertainty (about something); a particular instance of such disbelief or uncertainty.
doubt.e: I have doubts about how to convert this code to JavaScript.

download.d: A file transfer to a given computer or device from a remote one through a network connection.
download.e: The download took longer than I expected.

downtown.d: The main business part of a city or town, usually located at or near its center.
downtown.e: John walked every day to his downtown job.

drawer.d: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.

dressed.d: To fit out with the necessary clothing; to clothe, put clothes on (something or someone).
dressed.e: He was dressed in the latest fashions.

drill.d: A tool used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.
drill.e: Wear safety glasses when operating an electric drill.

drug.d: A substance used to treat an illness, relieve a symptom, or modify a chemical process in the body for a specific purpose.
drug.e: Aspirin is a drug that reduces pain, acts against inflammation and lowers body temperature.

duck.d: To quickly lower the head or body in order to prevent it from being struck by something.

during.e: I lived with my parents during the 1970s.

earn.d: To gain (success, reward, recognition) through applied effort or work.
earn.e: You can have the s'mores: you earned them, clearing the walkway of snow so well.

earring.d: A piece of jewelry worn on the ear.

earth.d: The third planet of the Solar System; the world upon which humans live.
earth.e: This is good earth for growing potatoes.

earthquake.d: A shaking of the ground, caused by volcanic activity or movement around geologic faults.

easily.e: Individuals without a family network are easily controlled.

east.d: One of the four principal compass points, specifically 90°, conventionally directed to the right on maps; the direction of the rising sun at an equinox. Abbreviated as E.

editor.d: A person who edits or makes changes to documents.

education.d: The process of imparting knowledge, skill and judgment.
education.e: Good education is essential for a well-run society.

educational.e: A school is an educational establishment.

effect.d: The result or outcome of a cause.
effect.e: The effect of the hurricane was a devastated landscape.

effort.d: The work involved in performing an activity; exertion.
effort.e: It took a lot of effort to find a decent-sized, fully-furnished apartment within walking distance of the office.   He made a conscious effort to not appear affected by the stories in the paper.

electric.d: (usually with definite article) Electricity; the electricity supply.
electric.e: We had to sit in the dark because the electric was cut off.

elephant.d: A mammal of the order Proboscidea, having a trunk, and two large ivory tusks jutting from the upper jaw.

embarrassing.d: present participle and gerund of embarrass

emergency.d: A situation which poses an immediate risk and which requires urgent attention.
emergency.e: Cardiac arrest is an emergency and if you find someone in cardiac arrest you should call 999 immediately.

empty.d: Devoid of content; containing nothing or nobody; vacant.

encourage.d: To mentally support; to motivate, give courage, hope or spirit.
encourage.e: We encourage the use of bicycles in the town centre.

endangered.d: To put (someone or something) in danger; to risk causing harm to.

ending.e: The book has a happy ending.

energetic.e: Cosmic rays are energetic particles from outer space.

enormous.d: Deviating from the norm; unusual, extraordinary.

enough.e: Are you man enough to fight me?

entertainment.d: An activity designed to give pleasure, enjoyment, diversion, amusement, or relaxation to an audience, no matter whether the audience participates passively as in watching opera or a movie, or actively as in games.

episode.d: An incident, action, or time period standing out by itself, but more or less connected with a complete series of events.
episode.e: It was a most embarrassing episode in my life.

escape.d: The act of leaving a dangerous or unpleasant situation.
escape.e: The prisoners made their escape by digging a tunnel.

essay.d: (authorship) A written composition of moderate length, exploring a particular issue or subject.

establish.d: To make stable or firm; to confirm.

evidence.d: Facts or observations presented in support of an assertion.
evidence.e: There is no evidence that anyone was here earlier.

exactly.e: He divided the coins exactly in half.

exam.e: He examined the crime scene for clues.

exchange.d: An act of exchanging or trading.
exchange.e: All in all, it was an even exchange.

exist.d: (stative) to be; have existence; have being or reality

expect.d: To predict or believe that something will happen
expect.e: He never expected to be discovered.

experience.d: The effect upon the judgment or feelings produced by any event, whether witnessed or participated in; personal and direct impressions as contrasted with description or fancies; personal acquaintance; actual enjoyment or suffering.
experience.e: It was an experience he would not soon forget.

explain.d: To make plain, manifest, or intelligible; to clear of obscurity; to illustrate the meaning of.
explain.e: To explain a chapter of the Bible.

explore.d: An exploration; a tour of a place to see what it is like.
explore.e: The committee has been exploring alternative solutions to the problem at hand.

express.d: A mode of transportation, often a train, that travels quickly or directly.
express.e: I took the express into town.

expression.d: The action of expressing thoughts, ideas, feelings, etc.

extra.d: Something additional, such as an item above and beyond the ordinary school curriculum, or added to the usual charge on a bill.
extra.e: Extra, extra! Read all about it!

fact.d: Something actual as opposed to invented.
fact.e: Gravity is a fact, not a theory.

fairly.d: In a fair manner; fair; not biased or skewed or favouring a certain party.
fairly.e: A jury is expected to ensure that the accused is fairly judged.
